forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED NO. The Islamabad Talks (the 21-hour negotiation with named US/Iran principals including Araghchi and Witkoff) were held April 11-12 2026 — before the F1 window (created June 2). Within the F1 window (to EOD June 16): the US and Iran reached a 'final agreed-upon text' on June 12, but this was via document exchange and relay through Pakistan/Qatar mediators, not a convened face-to-face or formally structured indirect session as required by the resolution criteria. Pakistan's PM Sharif announced the text agreement June 14; VP Vance confirmed the MOU was digitally co-signed June 14-15. The Versailles formal signing by Trump and Pezeshkian occurred June 17 — after the June 16 horizon. Per ambiguity_rule: 'written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.' No Iranian MFA statement formally rescinding the June 1 suspension was issued before EOD June 16. Resolves NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED YES. The June 17 Versailles ceremony constitutes a face-to-face, formally convened session between named US principal (President Trump) and named Iranian principal (President Pezeshkian), with French President Macron as G7 host. Multiple TIER1 sources confirm: NPR ('U.S. and Iran announce initial deal'), Al Jazeera ('Iran, US presidents sign deal'), CNN ('US releases official agreement'), Reuters and AP confirming the June 17 Versailles event. The session falls within the F2 window (June 10-24) and satisfies all resolution criteria: named principals, formal setting, TIER1 confirmation. The resolution_criteria does not restrict mediator to Oman/Pakistan/Qatar; a named host (France/G7) qualifies as a formally convened setting.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: Major downward revision. The June 7-8 bilateral exchange (CNN/TIER1 confirmed as worst strikes in months) predates the F3 window (opens June 10). Within the window June 10-24: Israeli strikes on Iranian targets continued through June 13-14, but US intervention blocked Iranian counter-strike; no TIER1-confirmed bilateral 48h exchange (both directions) is documented June 10-21. The June 15 Trump/Iran initial agreement and June 17 Versailles MOU established a 60-day ceasefire that took effect immediately. Remaining window June 21-24: near-zero risk given the active MOU ceasefire, US security guarantees to both parties, and stated commitments. Kept ACTIVE until June 24 horizon close; expected to resolve NO at expiry.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: Islamabad MOU (June 17) requires Hormuz to reopen toll-free within 30 days and Iran to clear mines within 30 days; US naval blockade lifted June 18. However: June 18 saw only 26 vessels transit (single-day, not a 7-day average); June 19-21 returned to near-zero as Lebanon fighting disrupted ceasefire implementation and insurer confidence. ~550 vessels remain stranded; analysts estimate 4+ months to full normalization; P&I war-risk insurance has not been reinstated; mine-clearing operations (active since April) have not opened a cleared commercial lane. Reaching 50/day 7-day average by July 2 (11 days from today) requires sustained daily throughput at 53% of pre-war baseline starting immediately — structurally implausible.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED YES. CENTCOM confirmed April 11 that USS Frank E. Peterson, USS Michael Murphy (DDGs), Avenger-class minesweepers from Sasebo, and UUV Mk18 commenced MCM operations in the Strait of Hormuz. The Hill confirmed 'US military starts removing mines from Strait of Hormuz amid shaky Iran ceasefire.' Active MCM operations are confirmed as ongoing and within the July 10 horizon. DA raised ambiguity that commencement (April 11) predates the resolution window (June 10 - July 10); Judge rules RESOLVED-YES: the resolution criteria ask whether operations 'actively commence' before EOD July 10 — they are confirmed active and ongoing within the window. The perverse alternative reading (active operations don't 'commence' in-window) is rejected. The Islamabad MOU also creates a new 30-day Iran obligation to clear mines, intensifying the operational phase post-June 17.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: A Times of Israel source (mid-June) reported the election is likely to be held on the original October 27 mandatory date, and that the dissolution bill is unlikely to pass its final readings. No second or third reading has been scheduled as of June 21. Parliamentary recess expected July 16, leaving ~3 weeks for two readings. Netanyahu-UTJ/Shas date disagreement (October vs September) remains unresolved. The Islamabad MOU ceasefire and active nuclear negotiation track reduce the political incentive to force early dissolution in the next 3 weeks. The dissolution bill's final passage requires 61 votes and a fixed date — neither is confirmed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Sunday cold-start review (cold-start p_cold = 0.22; gap from inherited 0.35 = 13pp; Judge selects 0.25 as partial cold-start credit). Coalition currently at approximately 60 seats: UTJ's ministers left government in July 2025 but Shas left government positions while remaining in coalition; effective supporting majority is at 60, one seat below the 61 threshold. However, the F7 resolution criteria requires a 'roll-call vote confirming coalition loss of majority' or 'Netanyahu announces early dissolution with date earlier than 2026-10-27.' The mandatory October 27 election date means dissolution will occur — but this does not satisfy the criteria unless the announced date is earlier than October 27. A Times of Israel source reported mid-June that the dissolution bill is unlikely to pass final readings and the election is expected on October 27. Wartime-consolidation dynamic (Islamabad MOU, active nuclear negotiations) removes near-term political pressure for Smotrich or Ben-Gvir to exit. Cold-start derivation at 0.22 is consistent with this reading.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed formal US-Iran nuclear negotiating session convene in Switzerland (or equivalent third-country venue) before EOD 2026-07-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast replacing resolved F2. Witkoff and Araghchi both traveled toward Switzerland June 18-19 for the first nuclear-phase talks; Vance canceled his trip; Switzerland confirmed the Burgenstock session was canceled June 19 after Lebanon fighting disrupted ceasefire implementation. Qatar's PM al-Thani had already arrived in Switzerland as mediator. A renewed Israel-Hezbollah truce was agreed June 19 (US-mediated) but IDF struck southern Lebanon after the 4pm deadline. The 60-day MOU creates time-pressure incentive; Qatar is positioned; both principals had already begun traveling — but Lebanon ceasefire fragility is the primary gating variable as of June 21.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports Witkoff (or named successor US envoy) and Araghchi (or named Iranian FM) convene a formal negotiating session on Iran's nuclear program in Switzerland or another named third-country venue, between 2026-06-21 and 2026-07-05.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNN/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement confirming a held session also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Travel toward venue without a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; preparatory technical meetings without named principals = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; postponement announcement without rescheduling = forecast stays ACTIVE.
